incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=control-plane metric=p99_latency path=/inference/streaming value=1.32s threshold=0.5s — paging oncall: SRE oncall
maria: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~260ms but p99 ~1.3s for streaming tails, started ~03:12 UTC. :fire:
kai: grabbing runtime traces. any recent deploys to control-plane or feature flags?
devon: product didn't push anything unusual. rolling evals earlier but no rollout.
aj: infra deploys: nothing to control-plane since 02:45. but configstore showed higher read QPS to redis and our tokenstore spiking.
maria: stacktrace from proxy looks like waiting on config-fetch + auth check for many requests. suspect featureflag fanout hitting configstore DB hotkeys.
ops-bot: db-read-replicas: cpu=92% connections=1865 — possible hot-shard. auth-rate-limiter: 429 spikes observed
nate: customer impact: streaming clients observed stalls and aborted streams. early estimate ~6-9% requests affected for hosted tier.
kai: quick query: top config keys by rps in last 5m
kai: ```
SELECT key, count(*) as rps FROM config_reads WHERE ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY key ORDER BY rps DESC LIMIT 10;
-- results: ff:experiment_banner_v2:region=us-east = 4200 rps, ff:user_layout_cache = 2700 rps
```
maria: that matches a hotkey (experiment_banner_v2) going crazy, likely due to a canary generating lots of reads per request.
aj: putting emergency rate-limit on configstore reads per-key to 1000rps. applying now.
aj: `kubectl apply -f emergency-configrate.yaml` -> `Applied` :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rolling configstore rate-limit patch to 3 pods
maria: enabling local fallback cache for control-plane path to short-circuit featureflag fetches for streaming endpoints.
kai: command to flip flag in runtime:
```
POST /admin/flags/override
{"path": "/inference/streaming", "flags": {"feature_flag_evaluation": "local_cache"}}
```
maria: applied. observed immediate drop in configstore qps for the hot key from 4.2k -> 350 rps.
ops-bot: db-read-replicas: connections now 820 cpu=48% — load dropped. nice.
devon: customer impact update: retries reduced, aborts down to ~1.5% after mitigation. still seeing p99 ~720ms, p95 ~220ms.
kai: tracing shows remaining latency coming from auth tokenstore internal calls — tokenstore had backpressure and some paths still waiting for refreshes.
nate: temporary mitigation: increase token cache TTL on proxy from 10s -> 60s to reduce auth RPCs for short-lived streams.
aj: TTL change rolled out in edge proxies. patch id: ttl-60s-rollback-safe
maria: routing fallback: for clients hitting p99 repeatedly we enabled model-variant fallback to smaller kv-friendly variant to avoid long generator warms (manual routing rule).
maria: current numbers: p95=210ms p99=320ms for non-affected routes, streaming tails for previously affected cohort now ~430ms. overall 99th still above SLO but customer errors reduced.
kai: can we avoid configstore reads hitting DB hot key in longer term? suggestion: shard flag keys by app id and introduce local in-memory LRU for hot keys.
aj: created follow-up ticket INF-7423: shard featureflag keys + per-key throttling + telemetry. assign eng-platform.
sophia: I'm taking second-shift handoff. summary: root cause = feature-flag canary causing configstore hotkey fanout -> DB and tokenstore backpressure -> streaming tail latency. Mitigations applied: emergency per-key rate-limit, local fallback cache for streaming path, token cache TTL bump, model-variant fallback routing. Customer impact: partial (6-9% -> ~1-2%) requests; no major loss but degraded SLOs around peak windows. Next steps: infra patch to auto-throttle featureflag bursters, review canary traffic shaping, postmortem and customer comms draft.
sophia: handing to oncall for 03:30-11:30 shift. full notes and runbook pinned to #incidents-docs. :pager:
maria: leaving notes: logs and trace links: https://internal-traces/redwood/2931122334
maria: also adding command snippets and timings to postmortem. thanks team. :heart:
incident-bot: Incident 2931122334 -> severity=sev2 (SLO degraded, customer impact) acknowledged by maria; open until resolved.
